name: Truncated Taylor method (JVP)
plain: Second-order truncated Taylor method: it takes the total derivative of the denoiser along the trajectory with forward-mode autodiff, instead of a second model call or history. Same formula as the k-diffusion TTM idea. Needs a model that supports torch.func.jvp.
math:
ε=(x−x0)/σ. x0′ = JVP of model(x,σ) along (−σε, −σ). h=log(σᵢ/σᵢ₊₁), h_η=h(η+1).
x ← e^{−h_η}x + (1−e^{−h_η})x0 + φ₂x0′, plus noise σᵢ₊₁√(1−e^{−2hη})·n·s_noise.
φ₂ = e^{−h}+h in extra_samplers.py; φ₂ = e^{−h_η}+h_η in other_samplers/sample_ttm.py.

providers.author: endman100
providers.note: Two near-identical bodies with different φ₂ when η≠0
